intro_1: Welcome back. Encabulation. Few words carry such weight.
intro_2: Since the first Encabulator was switched on, in a converted dairy outside Wolverhampton in nineteen twenty-eight, nobody has been entirely sure what it does. But everyone agrees it must keep on doing it.
intro_3: Today, an Encabulator stands quietly behind almost everything you rely on. The railways. The shipping forecast. The tides, quite possibly. You will never see one, which is how you know they're working.
intro_4: On day one, yesterday, we covered the cold start and the basic safety procedures. Today we build on those lessons, with the standard Encabulation procedure. If you understood day one, this will be perfectly easy. And you did understand it. I was there.
cue_001: So. Let's begin. Turn on the incoming isolator. That's the switch in the metal box to the left of the machine.
cue_002: Excellent. The delta readout on the main bus controller now shows zero point seven two. Normal operation. Now, as we practised yesterday, reboot the betaform amplifier.
cue_003: Hmm. That's the right switch. Try switching the oil pump off, and then on again. The LUBE OIL PUMP handle. Off first. Then on.
cue_004: There. Back to normal. Neumann Dynamik equipment is designed for absolute reliability. Occasionally it simply needs reminding. That is why we have a procedure. Follow the procedure, and you can rely on the machine.
cue_005: Oh. That's not good, is it?
cue_006: No, that's not supposed to happen. Could you have a look inside the Automation cabinet?
cue_007: Are you suicidal? Those boards are live. We covered this yesterday. Switch off the isolator in that cabinet first.
cue_008: Really not good. Would you mind having a poke around in there? Have a look at what might have blown.
cue_009: I thought I smelled something awful. Those are Pepperdyne modial-interaction boards in our hydrocoptic phase-control backplane... pull one out. I literally can't believe it.
cue_010: A Pepperdyne betaform amplifier. A modial-interaction board.
cue_011: Who put this here? Shoddy, second-rate goods. Honestly, this kind of thing gets good people killed.
cue_012: Get rid of it. I can't stand to even look at it. Horrible, insidious, evil thing. Pernicious. Stop the rot now.
cue_013: Good riddance to bad rubbish. Now get rid of the others. Tear them all out! One at a time. Let's show Pepperdyne what we think of their modial-interaction boards!
cue_015: It's pure evil. It's like a dark stain on the soul of the universe. Can't you see? It's sucking the energy out of our lives.
cue_016: You can't let this thing come between us.
cue_017: I thought we had something... you and me.
cue_018: A rapport, you know, a friendship.
cue_019: I think I saw something in you. Admittedly, from the moment I saw you, you seemed a bit different.
cue_020: A bit odd... but everybody in Encabulation is.
cue_021: Most people have no idea what we do.
cue_022: It's a calling, really. What would I be doing if I couldn't Encabulate?
cue_023: But, see, that's what I mean. That's why it's important you get rid of these disgusting, dirty Pepperdyne modial-interaction boards.
cue_024: Two down, three to go... you can do it. I have faith in you.
cue_025: Yes, faith. That's really what this was ever about. Trust.
cue_026: Who do you trust to encabulate? Turbo or Retro... it was always Neumann that I wanted to work for. First time I laid eyes on the powder-blue cabinets.
cue_027: Some say baby blue... like a newborn baby.
cue_028: This Encabulator is like a child to me.
cue_029: Like a sick, wounded child. Please, you're the doctor. We have to operate. There are three more Pepperdyne modial-interaction boards in my baby's heart.
cue_030: Yes, I can see the colour returning to its displays.
cue_031: You know, I knew something was out of the ordinary.
cue_032: It seemed almost sulky, like it was trying to tell me something.
cue_034: It would probably say, put this shard of villainy in the skip.
cue_035: Please, if not for me, then for it.
cue_036: I know it can sense us.
cue_039: Thank you. On behalf of me, this beautiful machine, and all of Neumann Dynamik, thank you.
cue_040: I know it's hard for you, and it's a lot to ask, but can you remove one more? It's only the hydrocoptic phase regulator.
cue_041: I know you're new on the job, and we wouldn't normally ask somebody to do a job like this until at least day three of the training... but you're all we've got.
cue_042: You've got this. Just reach into the cabinet, locate the hydrocoptic phase regulator, and give it a gentle tug and a slight twist to the right. You'll know it when you feel the click.
cue_043: Now don't be scared. We have faith in you.
cue_044: The management have faith in you.
cue_045: After today, you'll be a hero.
cue_046: They'll pin a medal to your chest.
cue_049: The glory... I wish it could be me.
cue_050: But I'll have the knowledge that I was there with you.
cue_051: And you'll remember that I was with you all the way.
cue_054: To think this morning we were strangers, and now look at us.
cue_055: It's true what they say about friendship in times of adversity, isn't it?
cue_056: Friends... yes, that's what we are.
cue_058: You did it, you bloody genius.
cue_059: Yeah, hot dang, you did it.
cue_060: They said you couldn't... I mean, you wouldn't.
cue_061: That you weren't the kind of person who could handle pressure.
cue_062: That you aren't the sort of person who can handle the heat.
cue_063: Keep up with the pace, you know, that sort of thing.
cue_064: Who? Doesn't really matter now, because they were wrong.
cue_065: We proved them wrong. You and me.
cue_066: Team. You, me, and the machine... oh, the machine.
cue_067: Wait, look at the machine... its lights are going out...
cue_070: After all we've been through... after all this struggle.
cue_071: Please save it. I know you have what it takes.
cue_072: One more card... I know you can do it.
cue_077: What's that? I think it's trying to say something.
cue_079: That we did our best, and it doesn't blame us for what happened.
cue_080: That it lived a good and blameless life.
cue_081: No, I won't let you go.
cue_082: It can't end like this. You're still under warranty.
cue_083: Quickly, the last card, the Baltovsky flux compensator, in the skip.
cue_085: Look at that. The lights are holding.
cue_086: That, trainee, was a job well done. A job very well done.
cue_087: I'm no doctor... well, I'm an Encabulation engineer, which is very nearly the same thing... and in my professional opinion...
cue_089: Oh, thank goodness. Thank goodness. I don't mind telling you, there was a moment back there when I thought we'd lost it.
cue_091: Normal operation. That's it. Now we can recalibrate the helical flange pellets. If you'd like to turn your attention to the—
cue_093: No, no, no. Come on. Come on, old thing.
cue_096: Stop all the clocks, cut off the telephone, Prevent the dog from barking with a juicy bone, Silence the pianos and with muffled drum Bring out the coffin, let the mourners come. Let aeroplanes circle moaning overhead Scribbling on the sky the message 'It is Dead'. Put crepe bows round the white necks of the public doves, Let the traffic policemen wear black cotton gloves. It was my North, my South, my East and West, My working week and my Sunday rest, My noon, my midnight, my talk, my song; I thought that love would last forever: I was wrong. The stars are not wanted now; put out every one, Pack up the moon and dismantle the sun, Pour away the ocean and sweep up the wood; For nothing now can ever come to any good.
cue_097: You think all this is a bit unhinged? Think I'm overreacting? I've seen good men go to their death. I've seen legions mown down. I've seen the killing fields of applied industrial engineering. So before you go telling me that I'm overreacting, tell that to the wives and widows of the men who lost everything... who gave everything.
cue_098: Every moment we let this filth operate, we let the criminals win. Somebody has to take a stand.
cue_099: All it takes for evil to prevail is for good men to do nothing.
cue_100: Why don't I do it? You have no idea the sacrifices I've made for the cause.
cue_101: What more evidence do you need that these things are evil?
cue_102: Throw it away, get rid of it!
cue_103: What are you thinking? Sullying our beautiful Encabulator with this filth! Our pristine, perfect, innocent Encabulator, soiled and besmirched with this foreign muck... No, don't you dare. Keep it away from my Encabulator.
cue_104: Litterbug! Honestly. If there's one thing I can't stand, it's littering. Littering! In a place this special.
cue_105: The skip. Over there. Big, yellow, you can't miss it.
cue_106: Pick it up, you slob, and put it in the skip.
cue_107: Yes, the skip, you dolt. Pick it up and put it in there.
cue_108: Go on then, what are you waiting for... pull it. Take out the trash.

betaform_intro: Oh. I see. Yesterday didn't happen for you, did it. It happened for me. I was there. Fine. The betaform amplifier reboot.
betaform_outro: There. That's all it is. That's all it ever was.
betaform_done: Lovely. Just as we rehearsed. Now, prime the oil pump. Turn the LUBE OIL PUMP handle to ON.
betaform_ack_3: Look at you. Just like yesterday.
betaform_isolator_say: Cycle the drive isolator. Off, and on again.
betaform_isolator_remind: The drive isolator. Under the drive, second section from the right. The red handle. Off. And then, and this is the part people forget, on again.
betaform_speed_say: Turn the speed knob on the drive all the way up.
betaform_speed_remind: The speed knob. On the drive. All the way up. Clockwise. The way clocks go. You've seen a clock.
betaform_fan_say: Put the panendermic fan on high.
betaform_fan_remind: The panendermic fan, in the far right-hand section. The selector. High. Not low. Not off. High. We sang a little song about it.
betaform_key_say: Turn the hydraulic pump key to local.
betaform_key_remind: The hydraulic pump. Third section along, the little key. Turn it to local. You did this yesterday. You had a biscuit. You held the biscuit in your other hand.
betaform_boost_say: Press boost on the panendermic fan.
betaform_boost_remind: The blue button. On the panendermic fan. It says boost. It has always said boost. Press it until it is blue.
betaform_phase_say: Set the phase selector on main incoming to the left.
betaform_phase_remind: Main incoming. The very first cabinet, at the top. The little selector beside the meters. Turn it to the left. All the way. It won't hurt.
betaform_kirk_say: Turn off the Kirk key on the main disconnect.
betaform_kirk_remind: The Kirk key. On the main disconnect. It's a key, in a lock, called Kirk. Turn it off. Nobody knows who Kirk was. We don't talk about Kirk.
betaform_hoa_say: Put the feed motor into hand.
betaform_hoa_remind: The feed motor. Second section, in the middle. The hand off auto switch. Turn it all the way round to hand. Like waving goodbye.
betaform_test_remind: The annunciator. The panel of little windows, under the main disconnect. Press test. They all light up. Everyone loves that bit. You loved that bit yesterday.
betaform_stop_say: Press the emergency stop on the auxiliary motor, then pull it out again.
betaform_stop_remind: The big red mushroom, on the auxiliary motor. Second section, at the bottom. Push it in. Then pull it out again. It is not an emergency. It is never an emergency.
reset_prompt: Now. The reset. The blue button, on the front of the automation control cabinet. Press it. Gently. It's been through a lot.
reset_remind: The blue button. Automation control. Reset. Please. For all of us.
skip_appears: Were you born in a barn? Put it away in the proper receptacle. There's a skip over there.
startup_main: Good. Now turn on the machine's main power. Turn the red handle marked MAIN DISCONNECT to ON.
startup_main_reset: The isolator is on. Now switch the machine's MAIN DISCONNECT off, then on again. Isolator first, main power second.
normal_extra: Just one final adjustment before we prime the hydrocoptic pump.
normal_done: Lovely. Just as we rehearsed. Now, prime the hydrocoptic pump.
